newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul said probing government projects over scandal.
newsitem.headline: Seoul said probing government projects over scandal.

text.p: South Korean prosecutors have begun probing government projects to find out if President Kim Young-sam's son accepted kickbacks in return for peddling influence, state radio said on Sunday.

Korea Broadcasting System (KBS) said state prosecutors had confirmed that a local construction company deposited more than one billion won ($1.12 million) in a bank account suspected of being opened on behalf of the president's son Kim Hyun-chul.
"The prosecution is focusing its probe on whether the money was a kickback in connection with a large government construction project," KBS said.
Prosecution officials were not available for comment on Sunday.

Kim Hyun-chul, the second son of the president, is under investigation over allegations that he meddled in state affairs, kept part of unspent funds from his father's election campaign in 1992, and played a role in a loans-for-kickbacks scandal involving failed Hanbo Steel Co.

Last week, a prosecution spokesman said prosecutors could not find any link between Kim Hyun-chul and the Hanbo scandal but had secured enough evidence to charge him this month over "irregularities unrelated to Hanbo".
The younger Kim has denied any links with Hambo Steel, which collapsed in January, revealing a web of corrupt alliances between politicians, businessmen and bankers.

Prosecutors have said they have secured evidence that executives of several companies looked after large sums of money linked to Kim Hyun-chul's associates, but have been unable to confirm the sources of the funds.

The influential Chosun Ilbo daily said prosecutors believed construction units of five to six business conglomerates, or chaebol, also deposited hundreds of millions of won in accounts controlled by associates of Kim Hyun-chul.
It said investigators had tried to establish if the money was paid after the companies won government projects.
The daily said prosecutors had also investigated medium-sized Dae Ho Construction Co, which had secured government orders worth more than 10 billion won since 1993 when President Kim took office.

Prosecutors have said they are trying to convince Lee Song-ho, former president of Dae Ho Construction and one of the junior Kim's close associates, to return home from the United States to help their probe.
Chosun Ilbo said prosecutors would summon Kim Hyun-chul this week and was likely to take legal action before May 20.

The main opposition National Congress for New Politics has alleged Kim Hyun-chul, who helped engineer his father's 1992 election victory, pressured banks to keep loans rolling into Hanbo Steel in return for a donation worth tens of billions of won to help finance the 1992 campaign. (US$1 = 894 won)
